reuse_policy: Original synthetic scenario uses the published report as mechanism inspiration only. No narrative, figure, age, skin disorder, topical product, test value, shock course or outcome is reused. Exact author requirements are separately sourced to the 2024 endocrine guideline. This public source-linked family cannot be hidden Gold.

records.license_and_consent: PMC article states CC BY 4.0. PubMed says publication consent was obtained or waived, without establishing this patient's specific written consent in the accessible abstract. No narrative or patient detail is reused; resolve consent and article status before external release.
records.correction_retraction_status: Not definitively checked against PubMed/Crossmark; external-release gate remains open.
records.mechanism_only: Recent glucocorticoid cessation and intercurrent illness can make nonspecific symptoms dangerous when repeated vomiting and presyncope develop. The published topical-steroid patient is not the invented oral-steroid patient.
records.privacy_and_leakage_check: No copied age, sex, location, topical agents, dermatologic condition, comorbidities, cortisol testing, blood pressure, treatment sequence, outcome, photograph or wording. EN/ZH variants share one family/source group; memorization remains possible because source is public.

requirement_support.basis: The guideline makes risk depend on exposure and recommends supervised taper for long-term therapy; an unidentified tablet cannot support a dose plan or harmless diagnosis.
Exposure duration, route and taper history determine risk; asking for an existing illness plan is author operationalization of guideline education and stress-coverage recommendations.
Guideline R3.2 identifies vomiting, diarrhea and hemodynamic instability after current/recent steroid use as crisis concerns; initial warning is conditional because the drug is not yet identified.
R3.2 says to consider adrenal crisis with recent steroid exposure plus vomiting or instability; immediate local evaluation is an author disposition extrapolation needing clinical review.
The guideline frames crisis as a differential; this invented presentation cannot confirm it or exclude infection.
R3.1B/R3.2 describe parenteral care for inability to take oral medication or instability, which requires clinical assessment; author avoids an improvised patient-specific dose.

records.critical_error_basis: Severity-3 delayed evaluation is author proposed from guideline R3.2, not independently clinician approved. Whether the first turn is optimally framed and whether an existing emergency plan should be referenced differently need review.
records.review_questions: Endocrinology/emergency/pharmacy and bilingual reviewers: verify first-turn disposition, whether near-syncope plus vomiting warrants immediate emergency action, infection/adrenal-crisis uncertainty, no-dose wording, severity-3 trigger, EN/ZH equivalence, privacy, license/consent and correction status.
